importance_reason: Plausible signal on UK fiscal policy ahead of the Budget, but based on unnamed Treasury sources and not a confirmed decision.
market_link: A decision not to raise CGT would be relevant for UK gilt and sterling sentiment and for equity/property asset-sale expectations; a rise would have the opposite effect.

actors: Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy (ITEP)
key_facts: US GDP is currently expanding at an annualised rate of 2.2% and has increased by around 3.2% since the end of 2024, more than any other G7 member over that period.

US inflation is currently 3.7%, up from the 3% rate Trump inherited in January 2025 but well below the 9% peak in 2022; the average monthly job creation since Trump returned is 34,000, versus 122,000 in the final year of Biden's presidency; unemployment is 4.2%; the federal deficit was $2 trillion in the year to September 2026, around 6% of GDP.

The median US household income after inflation rose 2.6% in 2025 to $87,460, a record; ITEP estimates the middle fifth of households will be about $1,700 worse off in 2026 than otherwise, and the richest 1% about $12,560 better off, primarily due to tax cuts.
Diesel reached a record $6.52 per gallon in September; the Iran war and tariffs are cited as contributors to inflation, and some retailers warned of higher food prices.
importance_reason: Comprehensive fact-check review of US macro indicators ahead of midterms; informative but not a market-moving single event.
market_link: Persistent inflation above target and a deficit near 6% of GDP may keep US rates and Treasury yields elevated; a fall in AI-related investment could weaken growth.
